description: Remove one or more paths. Request shape: {"paths": ["..."]}. Directories need `recursive: true`; missing paths are idempotent successes; recursive removal refuses to descend through non-accessible entries. Paths are relative to the primary allowed root or absolute inside any allowed root (coder::info lists them); for host paths outside the jail use shell::fs::*.

paths.description: Paths to remove. Each entry is relative to the primary allowed root, or an absolute path inside any allowed root. Call `coder::info` to see the allowed roots. Paths outside every allowed root are rejected — use the shell worker's `shell::fs::*` for host paths outside the jail.

recursive.description: Required for non-empty directories. Files and empty dirs ignore it.

error.description: Structured error for this entry. `code` is stable for programmatic branching (e.g. `"C211"` for not-found-or-denied; `"C210"` for refusing to delete an allowed root). `message` carries the corrective action an LLM agent needs to make a successful second call.

path.description: Canonical absolute path (resolved through the jail); the caller's input verbatim when resolution failed.

WireError.description:
Structured per-entry error as it appears on the wire.

Use `code` for stable programmatic branching (e.g. `"C211"` for not-found-or-denied). `message` carries the human/LLM-readable problem description plus the corrective next call.

code.description: Stable error code, e.g. "C211". See the README error table.

message.description: Human/LLM-readable message: problem + actual values + corrective next call.
